players.product: Turnkey HPC data-center campuses leased to hyperscalers (Barber Lake, Black Pearl, Stingray - Texas) - ex-Bitcoin-mining, now 'Cipher Digital'

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: revenue for the first quarter was $35 million, down from $60 million in Q4, reflecting the planned wind down of mining operations at Black Pearl (fully decommissioned in February) and the transition toward contracted data center revenue; GAAP net loss was $114 million, or $0.28 per diluted share, driven by lower revenue, a decrease in the fair value of the PPA and higher interest expense from the new debt facilities.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $35 million (vs $60 million in Q4); GAAP net loss $114 million, $0.28 per diluted share

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: signed a third data center campus lease this quarter - a 15-year initial term agreement with an unnamed investment-grade hyperscale tenant covering 100 MW ("As for the contract, no, it covers the 100 MW"), making three consecutive long-term leases in about eight months. Operating and contracted capacity is 907 MW (207 MW Bitcoin mining at Odessa, 300 MW Barber Lake with Fluidstack and Google, 300 MW Black Pearl with Amazon Web Services, 100 MW under the third lease), carrying approximately $11.4 billion in contracted revenue across base lease terms of 10-15 years.
quarterly_data.figure: 907 MW operating and contracted; approximately $11.4 billion contracted revenue; third lease 100 MW, 15-year initial term

capex.period: base lease terms of 10-15 years (as of Q1 FY2026 call)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the three executed data center campus leases are expected to generate approximately $787 million of average annualized net operating income from October 2026 to September 2036, and approximately $892 million of contracted net operating income in 2035 - contracted NOI from signed agreements with investment-grade counterparties, not projections based on assumed future leases.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $787 million average annualized NOI (October 2026 to September 2036); approximately $892 million contracted NOI in 2035

quarterly_data.signal: Barber Lake construction: the building topped out in April - 127 days from first column to last structural beam for a roughly 800,000 sq ft structure built to deliver 207 MW of critical IT load; approximately 99% of the required equipment is secured with delivery schedules aligned (supply-chain risk to the timeline 'minimal'), design is 100% complete, mechanical/electrical/networking workfronts are progressing in parallel toward contractual early access and substantial completion dates; over 1,100 daily active workers on site in April, more than 1,400 expected in May; tenants to be welcomed later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 99% of equipment secured; 207 MW of critical IT load; topped out in 127 days (roughly 800,000 sq ft)

quarterly_data.signal: Black Pearl: Bitcoin mining decommissioning is complete and the site has fully transitioned to data center development; phase I retrofit is installing cooling and electrical infrastructure so the legacy building can take HPC equipment, with approximately 93% of phase I equipment secured; phase II site layout and earthwork began in April, three months after design kickoff, with approximately 80% of phase II equipment secured. CEO: the outstanding items are not long-lead-time items but commodity-like items (cable, office furniture, miscellaneous mechanical equipment); the project is tracking to contractual early access and rack-ready dates across both phases.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 93% of phase I equipment secured; approximately 80% of phase II equipment secured

quarterly_data.signal: Stingray (Andrews County, Texas): 100 MW of gross capacity, fully approved, with a target energization date in the fourth quarter 2026; development began in Q1 with earthwork and pad preparation in progress and substation electrical work commenced; the CFO said construction mobilization at this third site begins in Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: 100 MW of gross capacity; target energization Q4 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline: approximately 3.3 GW of grid-capacity pipeline, approximately 4.2 GW of total portfolio grid power (roughly 78% pipeline HPC). Reveille (Cotulla, Texas) has ERCOT interconnection approval for 70 MW gross, below the batch-process threshold, energization Q3 2027, in advanced discussions with multiple potential tenants; Ulysses is a 200 MW site in southeastern Ohio (Cipher's first in PJM) targeting energization in Q4 2027, with live discussions with multiple hyperscalers; McLennan, Mikeska and Colchis are expected to energize in 2028 and to be in batch zero of the new ERCOT batch process (finalization expected in June); 2028-2029 sites add up to 2.5 GW; an additional 500 MW at Barber Lake is a 2030-and-beyond upsize opportunity. CEO aspiration: 4+ GW of HPC operating by 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 3.3 GW pipeline; up to 4.2 GW total portfolio; Reveille 70 MW gross (Q3 2027); Ulysses 200 MW (Q4 2027); up to 2.5 GW in 2028-2029

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing and business model: CEO says Cipher continues to see premium pricing in lease negotiations for near-term-available sites ("I do not see lease rates going down for premium sites with good timelines"). At the 70 MW Reveille site Cipher is evaluating structures where it would participate in owning and operating the compute for a neocloud tenant, citing investment-grade credit support and prepayments now available to neoclouds; colocation remains favored where elevated lease rates are available.

Financing: completed a $2 billion Black Pearl project bond at a 6.125% coupon (significantly oversubscribed, fully funding Black Pearl through delivery, including a reimbursement of approximately $233 million for prior equity contributions) - the third project-level bond; closed an inaugural $200 million four-year revolving credit facility at SOFR plus 125 to 175 basis points (undrawn at quarter end). Cipher Compute LLC (Barber Lake) carries approximately $1.7 billion of notes due November 2030. Total debt principal approximately $5.2 billion; unrestricted cash $715 million; Bitcoin $76 million; restricted construction cash approximately $3.5 billion. CFO: liquidity is sufficient to fund the near-term development pipeline without additional equity.
quarterly_data.figure: $2 billion bond at 6.125%; $200 million revolver; total principal approximately $5.2 billion; unrestricted cash $715 million; restricted cash approximately $3.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Odessa Bitcoin mining: operating 207 MW generating approximately 11.6 exahash per second at approximately 17.2 joules per terahash; mined approximately 346 Bitcoin in Q1 under a fixed-price PPA at approximately $0.028 per kWh that can run until the end of July 2027. No further capex into Bitcoin mining; CEO expects Bitcoin to be out of the story by end of 2027 at the latest. There is hyperscaler interest in Odessa and Cipher would be interested in converting it to an HPC campus as it did Black Pearl, which would require renegotiating the PPA.
quarterly_data.figure: 207 MW; approximately 11.6 exahash per second; approximately 346 Bitcoin mined; approximately $0.028 per kWh

quarterly_data.signal: Behind-the-meter power: CEO says some of Cipher's best people have spent most of their recent time on behind-the-meter on-site generation using cheap natural gas at its West Texas sites (engineering, gas infrastructure, IPPs, air permits and financing still to be solved) and called it possibly 'the most upside convexity potential in our stock', with tenants interested; no figure given.

contracts.signal: CEO lists 300 MW contracted at Barber Lake with Fluidstack and Google; the building topped out in April, approximately 99% of equipment is secured, and the project is tracking toward all contractual early access and substantial completion milestone dates, with tenants expected on campus later this year. The CFO noted a $44 million non-cash gain on the warrant liability reflecting the value of the Google warrants associated with the Barber Lake lease.

connects_to.relationship: Black Pearl (TX) AI/HPC data-center campus lease to Amazon Web Services

contracts.signal: CEO lists 300 MW contracted at Black Pearl with Amazon Web Services; Bitcoin mining at the site is decommissioned, phase I retrofit (approximately 93% of equipment secured) and phase II (approximately 80% secured, earthwork began in April) are tracking to contractual early access and rack-ready dates; fully funded by the $2 billion Black Pearl bond.
